paper_title: A Highly Planar Fluorinated Benzothiadiazole-Based Conjugated Polymer for High-Performance Organic Thin-Film Transistors
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2015 - Nketia‐Yawson - A Highly Planar Fluorinated Benzothiadiazole‐Based Conjugated Polymer for/auto/Advanced Materials - 2015 - Nketia‐Yawson - A Highly Planar Fluorinated Benzothiadiazole‐Based Conjugated Polymer for.md

knowledge_points.content: The conjugated polymer PDFDT is designed using a donor-acceptor (D-A) strategy combining electron-deficient difluorobenzothiadiazole (DFBT) and electron-rich dithienosilole moieties to achieve high backbone planarity and strong interchain interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: With these favorable features in mind, we attempted to combine difluorobenzothiadiazole and dithienosilole moieties to synthesize a semiconducting polymer while expecting high coplanarity of the resulting polymer backbone and strong π-π interactions.

knowledge_points.content: The introduction of fluorine atoms into the benzothiadiazole unit induces a planar geometry through F...S non-covalent attractive interactions and interchain C-H...F or C-F...π interactions, resulting in close π-π stacking distances of 3.4–3.8 Å.
knowledge_points.evidence: It is known that the replacement of hydrogens with fluorines can induce a planar geometry when fluorines are geometrically close to the neighboring thiophene moieties via F...S non-covalent attractive interaction... these enhance the planarity of polymer backbones further, resulting in quite close (3.4-3.8 A) π-π polymer chain stacking.

knowledge_points.content: The Si-C bond length (1.89 Å) in the dithienosilole unit is longer than the C-C bond length (1.53 Å) in cyclopentadiene, which facilitates more efficient interchain packing and stronger π-π interactions in the polymer.
knowledge_points.evidence: A key reason for these advantages is that the Si-C bond length (1.89 A) in the dithienosilole unit is longer than the C-C bond length (1.53 A) in the cyclopentadiene unit, allowing efficient interchain packing and strong π-π interactions.

knowledge_points.content: PDFDT-based top-gate/bottom-contact (TG/BC) OTFTs achieved a peak hole mobility of 9.0 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (average 6.6 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) when using the high-k ferroelectric dielectric P(VDF-TrFE).
knowledge_points.evidence: more impressively, a highest mobility of 9.0 cm2 V-1 s-1 (average 6.6 cm2 V-1 s-1) was recorded with P(VDF-TrFE) dielectrics.

knowledge_points.content: PDFDT exhibits a HOMO energy level of -5.24 eV and a LUMO energy level of -3.37 eV, with the HOMO level being lowered by 0.14 eV compared to non-fluorinated analogues due to the electron-withdrawing effect of fluorine.
knowledge_points.evidence: which corresponds to the HOMO and LUMO levels of -5.24 and -3.37 eV, respectively... The HOMO level was lowered by 0.14 eV due to the introduction of the electron-withdrawing fuorine atoms.

knowledge_points.content: Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXD) of PDFDT films reveals an unusually close π-π stacking distance of 3.42 Å, which is attributed to the highly planar backbone and strong interchain interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: another weak π-π stacking peak at 1.839 Å⁻¹ (3.42 Å)... Note that the very close (3.42 Å) π-π stacking has not been previously observed in the D-A-type conjugated polymers.

knowledge_points.content: The use of high-k ferroelectric gate insulators like P(VDF-TrFE) improves hole mobility in PDFDT OTFTs by inducing band bending through large dipole polarization at the dielectric-semiconductor interface, facilitating charge accumulation.
knowledge_points.evidence: The improvement in mobility is due to the induced band bending emanating from the large dipole polarization at the interface of the ferroelectric gate insulators and PDFDT polymer. This improves the accumulation of positive charges carriers, leading to a remarkable boost in hole mobility.

knowledge_points.content: Thermal annealing of PDFDT films at 150°C optimizes device performance by promoting the formation of a networked nanofiber morphology, which enhances charge carrier transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: The 150 °C annealed polymer films exhibited more uniform and more numerous grown nanofibers of networked polymer chains... The highly improved mobility by thermal annealing can be attributed to the tightly packed, fibrously well-connected nature of the polymer chains.

knowledge_points.content: PDFDT OTFTs demonstrate high bias-stress stability in both nitrogen and air, which is attributed to the low-lying HOMO level (-5.24 eV) that enhances oxidative stability.
knowledge_points.evidence: The devices showed good stability in both nitrogen and air owing to the lower HOMO level (-5.24 eV) of the PDFDT polymer... high bias-stress stability was obtained for PDFDT devices presumably because of the lower HOMO energy level.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations for PDFDT indicate an extremely flat monomeric structure with dihedral angles of 0° and a polymer backbone with dihedral angles around single bonds of less than 15°.
knowledge_points.evidence: Importantly, all the chemical structures were extremely flat, with dihedral angles of 0°... The molecular backbone appeared to be very flat, with dihedral angles around single bonds less than 15°.

knowledge_points.content: PDFDT films exhibit a face-on orientation relative to the substrate, evidenced by the observation of both lamellar (100) and π-π stacking peaks in the out-of-plane direction in GIXD patterns.
knowledge_points.evidence: This suggested that the polymer backbones lie parallel to the substrate with face-on orientation... the fact that both the lamellar spacing and the π-π stacking are pronounced in the same direction can be explained.
